subject: Multi-year lanes + optional auto-extend window for growth-triggered capacity
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmerobotics.com>, Acme Robotics Procurement <procurement@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Multi-year lanes + optional auto-extend window for growth-triggered capacity

Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. To recap what we discussed on the call and to move procurement forward, we propose structuring the renewal as:

- Three-year agreement with three "capacity lanes" (Base / Growth / Surge).
- Base is the committed baseline (year 1 volume). Growth lane scales at pre-agreed tier pricing when monthly usage exceeds X% of baseline.
- Surge lane is short-term burst capacity billed at a higher per-token rate with guaranteed provisioning SLA.
- Optional auto-extend window: 30-day opt-out each renewal year that auto-extends the current lane if both parties don't opt out. This is optional for Acme to accept — we can surface it as a checkbox in the agreement.

Key asks for you: can procurement confirm whether a 30-day opt-out is acceptable, and whether you want the surge trigger to be threshold-based (recommended) or ad-hoc approval?

Happy to send a one-page term summary and a DocuSign package for review. If helpful, I can also include a canary burst plan for the first 90 days of year 2.

Can we target a decision/feedback window by Tue 23 Jun so we can lock pricing for the quarter?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmerobotics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Acme Robotics Procurement <procurement@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Multi-year lanes + optional auto-extend window for growth-triggered capacity

Karthik —

Appreciate the summary. The structure looks promising. A couple quick procurement questions:

1) Auto-extend: procurement will need the opt-out language to be explicit (notice window, how notice is delivered, and whether partial opt-out is allowed across lanes).
2) Surge lane: we prefer a threshold-based trigger tied to a rolling 30-day average rather than one-off spikes. Can you propose a clear metric?
3) SLA credits: does Redwood provide credits if surge provisioning misses the SLA?

We'd like to see the one-page term summary and a sample DocuSign so legal can do a light redline. Procurement expects to review within ~2-3 weeks once we have the paper.

Cc'ing procurement directly so they see scope.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform, Acme Robotics
sam.patel@acmerobotics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Multi-year lanes + optional auto-extend window for growth-triggered capacity

Internal notes —

Marissa / Vanessa,

Sam asked specifically for: explicit opt-out language + rolling 30-day surge trigger + SLA credits for missed surge provisioning. Proposed defaults:

- Opt-out: 30 days notice via email to account team; applies per-lane (they can opt-out of Surge auto-extend but keep Growth).
- Surge trigger: 150% of baseline measured as a 30-day rolling average. We will define baseline as average monthly token usage across the last 90 days of the prior year or first-year monthly average (whichever they select).
- SLA: If surge provisioning latency > agreed SLA (20s median for initial ramp), provide a 10% credit on surge fees for that month, escalated remediation SLA 48 hours.

If you agree, I'll bake these into a one-page term summary and attach to the DocuSign. Any pushback on the 150% threshold or the 10% credit? If we lower threshold we risk more frequent surge billing which they'll likely contest.

Thanks — Karthik

Sam / procurement team —

Attached: redwood_term_summary_v2.pdf (one-page) and the DocuSign packet (acme_docsign_proposal_0626.pdf). Highlights in the packet:

- Multi-year lanes (3 years) with lane definitions and pricing bands.
- Opt-out mechanics: 30-day notice by email to account@redwood.com; opt-out available per-lane.
- Surge trigger: 150% rolling 30-day average of baseline (baseline definition included).
- SLA credits: 10% credit on surge fees for months where surge provisioning misses the agreed latency SLA; remediation commitment 48 hours.

Action items:
1) Please review the one-pager and the DocuSign. If procurement has a small redline, we can accept a single clause edit (SLA credit cap) before routing to legal.
2) If you approve, sign the DocuSign by Tue 23 Jun to keep pricing intact for Q3 onboarding.

If you'd like a 30-minute walk-through of the packet with Marissa and me, we can do Wed or Thu next week.

Karthik —

Good summary; procurement will review the packet today. Two quick asks before we sign:

1) Can we add a maximum monthly cap on cumulative surge credits (to limit Redwood exposure)? Procurement suggests a small cap tied to 20% of monthly surge fees.
2) Legal will likely redline the exact opt-out notification text — please allow us one edit and we'll get it back the same day.

If those are acceptable, we will route to DocuSign and aim to sign by Tue 23 Jun. Also please include Marissa on any walk-through invites so product can confirm the baseline calculation.

Thanks — Sam
